title: Pipeline operations
description: How much of the published archive this instance actually holds, and what the daily aggregates were computed from. Every panel reads the published aggregates or the record of ingested hours; none of them can read per-account rows, because the connection is not permitted to.

panels.title: Hours ingested
panels.description: Hours the ingest has converted and recorded. This is a count of rows in the record, not of files on disk — `reporadar verify` is what compares the two, and it exists because a completion record is only meaningful relative to the store it describes.

targets.rawSql: select count(*) as value from archive_hours where status = 'ingested'

panels.title: Hours outstanding
panels.description: Hours recorded as missing from the publisher or as failed. Not the same as unattempted: an hour nothing has looked at yet has no row at all, which is why the gap scan derives what is due from the calendar rather than from this table.

targets.rawSql: select count(*) as value from archive_hours where status in ('missing', 'failed')

panels.title: Hours since the newest ingested hour
panels.description: Freshness. The publisher releases an hour about five minutes after it closes, so a healthy always-on instance sits near one or two. A number that keeps climbing means the convergence loop is not running, not that hours are missing — the loop is level-triggered, so it recovers the whole gap on its next pass rather than needing a catch-up.

targets.rawSql: select extract(epoch from ((now() at time zone 'UTC') - max(day + make_interval(hours => hour)))) / 3600.0 as value from archive_hours where status = 'ingested'

panels.title: Events recorded
panels.description: Summed from the hours record rather than from the aggregates, so it stays a second, independent count of the same thing. When it exceeds the total charted below, the two are describing different stores: the hours record is one table shared by every run, while the columnar files it points at live under whichever data directory produced them. That is a real condition rather than a fault, and `reporadar verify` is what reports it precisely — a completion record only means something relative to the store it describes.

targets.rawSql: select coalesce(sum(events), 0) as value from archive_hours where status = 'ingested'

panels.title: Hours the record claims that the aggregates below do not cover
panels.description: Read this before anything under it. The aggregates are built by a command somebody runs; ingest converges on its own, so the two drift apart silently and every panel below keeps rendering — with numbers quietly smaller than the truth. Zero means what is charted covers every hour the record claims. Computed against the coverage each aggregate row carries, so it needs no note of when a build last ran: a build that finished a minute ago against a lake that has moved since is recent and stale at the same time. Anything above zero is closed one of two ways, and this panel cannot tell you which, because a database connection cannot see the files. If `reporadar verify` passes, it is a build that is owed, and `make marts-converge` runs it. If `verify` fails, the record is claiming hours the lake does not hold, no build can supply them, and `reporadar marts-status` is the one that reports the gap a rebuild would actually close.

targets.rawSql: select coalesce(sum(lake.hours - coalesce(built.hours_present, 0)), 0) as "hours not yet built from" from (select day, count(*) as hours from archive_hours where status = 'ingested' and events > 0 group by day) as lake left join marts.ecosystem_daily as built on built.day = lake.day where built.hours_present is null or built.hours_present < lake.hours

panels.title: Coverage — hours held per day, out of 24
panels.description: The panel to read before any of the others. A daily total computed from seven hours and one computed from twenty-four look identical in every chart except this one, so a dip here explains a dip everywhere else. It is read from the aggregates, which carry their own coverage rather than having it attached afterwards.

targets.rawSql: select day as time, hours_present as "hours held" from marts.ecosystem_daily where $__timeFilter(day) order by day

panels.title: Events, repositories and accounts per day
panels.description: Volume at the ecosystem grain. Compare against the coverage panel before reading a change as a change in GitHub rather than a change in how much of the day was ingested. Accounts are counted, never listed — per-account rows live in a schema this connection cannot read.

targets.rawSql: select day as time, events, repos as repositories, actors as accounts from marts.ecosystem_daily where $__timeFilter(day) order by day

panels.title: Most recent hours
panels.description: The record itself, newest first — what the aggregates above are derived from. An hour appears here once it has been attempted; its status is the current one, because an hour published late is re-recorded rather than left at its first answer.

targets.rawSql: select day, hour, status, events, bytes, detail, recorded_at from archive_hours order by day desc, hour desc limit 50
